definitions.explanation: A child-rearing approach of deliberately exposing a child to hardship to make them stronger. The image comes from the legend that a lion pushes its cub off a cliff and raises only the one that climbs back up.

examples.japanese: ⟦{獅子|しし}→獅子：04944_shishi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{子|こ}{落|お}としだ。
examples.english: It's tough love, like a lion pushing its cub off a cliff.

examples.japanese: ⟦{父|ちち}→父：00566_chichi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{子|こ}{落|お}とし⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦つもり→つもり：01152_tsumori⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{私|わたし}→私：02988_watashi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{遠|とお}く⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{学校|がっこう}→学校：00055_gakkou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{行|い}かせた→行く：00119_iku⟧。
examples.english: My father sent me to a distant school as a kind of tough love.

examples.japanese: ⟦{獅子|しし}→獅子：04944_shishi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{子|こ}{落|お}とし⟦の→の：09472_no⟧ような⟦{厳|きび}しい→厳しい：01125_kibishii⟧⟦{訓練|くんれん}→訓練：02673_kunren⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{乗|の}り{越|こ}えて→乗り越える：04620_norikoeru⟧⟦こそ→こそ：12731_koso⟧、⟦{本物|ほんもの}→本物：03628_honmono⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{力|ちから}→力：01661_chikara⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{身|み}→身：01764_mi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧つく。
examples.english: Only by overcoming a lion-style tough-love training does one acquire real strength.

notes:
Comes from the saying ⟦{獅子|しし}→獅子：04944_shishi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{我|わ}が→我が〜：03971_waga⟧⟦{子|こ}→子：09851_ko⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{千尋|せんじん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{谷|たに}→谷：02223_tani⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{落|お}とす→落とす：01246_otosu⟧ — "the lion drops its cub into a deep valley." Usually appears in the longer form ⟦{獅子|しし}→獅子：04944_shishi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{子|こ}{落|お}とし; the short form {子|こ}{落|お}とし is less common.

USAGE:
Describes a deliberately strict or harsh choice made out of belief that hardship strengthens the child. Carries a serious, sometimes admiring tone — not a casual term for ordinary discipline.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {可愛|かわい}い⟦{子|こ}→子：09851_ko⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{旅|たび}→旅：03407_tabi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦させよ→する：00392_suru⟧: send the cherished child on a journey — similar moral, gentler imagery
- ⟦スパルタ→スパルタ：22799_suparuta⟧⟦{教育|きょういく}→教育：01313_kyouiku⟧: Spartan upbringing — modern term for harsh training
